==English== {{wp|}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|keepe||obsolete}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|kēp}}, {{IPA|en|/kiːp/}} ** {{IPA|en|[kiːp]|[kʰɪjp]|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|[kʰɪjp]|a=SSB,Southern US}} ** {{IPA|en|[k̟çi(ː)p]|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|[k(ʰ)i(ː)p]|a=CA,Scotland}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-keep.wav|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-keep.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|en-au-keep.ogg|a=AU}} * {{rhymes|en|iːp|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|kepen|t=to keep, guard, look after, watch}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cēpan|t=to seize, hold, observe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kōpijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kōpijaną|t=to look, heed, watch, observe}} (compare {{cog|fy|kypje|t=to look}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵab-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*ǵāb-|t=to look after}} (compare {{cog|lt|žẽbti|t=to eat reluctantly}}, {{cog|ru|забо́та|t=care, worry}}). The dialectal {{l|en|keep|sense of the verb meaning “to put back” or “put away”|id=put-back}} may be analyzed as a {{glossary|semantic loan}} from a local language—compare {{ncog|cy|cadw}} and {{ncog|cmn|-}} {{zh-m|收|tr=shōu}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|kept}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[continue]] in (a course or mode of action); to not [[intermit]] or [[fall]] from; to [[uphold]] or [[maintain]]. #: {{ux|en|to '''keep''' silence;  to '''keep''' possession}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[remain]] [[faithful]] to a given [[promise]] or [[word]]. #: {{syn|en|fullfill|hold|honor}} #: {{ux|en|  to '''keep''' one's word;  to '''keep''' one's promise}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Twelfth Night|act=V|scene=i|passage=Both day and night did we '''keep''' company.}} #* {{RQ:Smollett Regicide|scene=v|page=70|passage=Within the Portal as I '''kept''' my Watch, / Swift gliding Shadows by the glimm'ring Moon, I could perceive in Forms of armed Men, / Poſſeſſ the Space that borders on the Porch— {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} {{non-gloss|To hold the status of something.}} ## To [[maintain]] [[possession]] of. ##: {{ux|en|I '''keep''' a small stock of painkillers for emergencies.}} ##: {{ux|en|I only meant to lend him the shirt at first, but it looked better on him than me, so I told him to '''keep''' it.}} ## {{label|en|ditransitive}} To [[maintain]] the [[condition]] of; to [[preserve]] in a certain [[state]]. ##: {{ux|en|I '''keep''' my specimens under glass to protect them.}} ##: {{ux|en|The abundance of squirrels '''kept''' the dogs running for hours.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=10|passage=Mr. Cooke had had a sloop yacht built at Far Harbor, the completion of which had been delayed, and which was but just delivered.{{...}}The Maria had a cabin, which was finished in hard wood and yellow plush, and accommodations for '''keeping''' things cold.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1935|author=[https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/288354.George_Goodchild George Goodchild] |title=Death on the Centre Court|chapter=1 |passage=She mixed furniture with the same fatal profligacy as she mixed drinks, and this outrageous contact between things which were intended by Nature to be '''kept''' poles apart gave her an inexpressible thrill.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[record]] [[transaction]]s, [[account]]s, or [[event]]s in. ##: {{ux|en|I used to '''keep''' a diary.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[enter]] ([[account]]s, [[record]]s, etc.) in a [[book]]. ## {{lb|en|archaic}} To [[remain]] in; to be [[confine]]d to. ##* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=12|book=II|passage=''Metrocles'' somewhat indiscreetly, as he was disputing in his Schole, in presence of his auditory, let a fart, for shame whereof he afterwards '''kept''' his house and could not be drawen abroad{{nb...}}.}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|act=III|scene=ii|passage=The wrathful skies / Gallow the very wanderers of the dark / And make them '''keep''' their caves.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1789|author={{w|John Moore (Scottish physician)|John Moore}}|title=Zeluco|publisher=Valancourt|year_published=2008|page=71 |passage=The following day she was so ill that she '''kept''' her bed; the husband went not once to enquire for her, nor did he send any message: he also '''kept''' his apartment, and was heard walking backwards and forwards with a hurried pace the whole of that day.}} ##* {{RQ:Doyle Poison Belt|passage="As I sat alone at my breakfast--Mrs. Challenger is in the habit of '''keeping''' her room of a morning--it suddenly entered my head that it would be entertaining and instructive to see whether I could find any limits to this woman's inperturbability."}} ## To [[restrain]]. ##: {{ux|en|I '''keep''' my pet gerbil away from my brother.}} ##: {{ux|en|Don't let me '''keep''' you; I know you have things to be doing.}} ## {{lb|en|with ''from''}} To [[watch over]], [[look after]], [[guard]], [[protect]]. ##: {{ux|en|May the Lord '''keep''' you from harm.}} ##* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=VIII|passage=cursse on thy cruell hond, / That twise hath sped; yet shall it not thee '''keepe''' / From the third brunt of this my fatall brond {{...}}}} ## To [[supply]] with [[necessity|necessities]] and [[financially]] [[support]] (a person). ##: {{ux|en|He '''kept''' a mistress for over ten years.}} ## {{lb|en|of living things}} To [[raise]]; to [[care]] for. ##: {{ux|en|He has been '''keeping''' orchids since retiring.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1828|author=w:Thomas Keightley|title=The Fairy Mythology|volume=I|location=London|publisher=William Harrison Ainsworth|page=287|passage=Here John had to '''keep''' cows with other boys, and they used to drive them to graze about the Nine-hills.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1914|author=Robert Joos|title=Success with Hens|publisher=Forbes & company|page=217 |passage=Of course boys are boys and need watching, but there is little watching necessary when they '''keep''' chickens.}} ##* {{RQ:Guardian|date=December 14, 2011|author=Steven Morris|title=Devon woman jailed for 168 days for killing kitten in microwave |url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2011/dec/14/woman-killed-kitten-microwave-jail |passage=Jailing her on Wednesday, magistrate Liz Clyne told Robins: "You have shown little remorse either for the death of the kitten or the trauma to your former friend Sarah Knutton." She was also banned from '''keeping''' animals for 10 years.}} ## To [[refrain]] from [[freely]] [[disclose|disclosing]] (a [[secret]]). ##* {{quote-song|en|author=Anthony Reyes; Melissa Sheppard|authorlabel=no|title=Leave the Lights On|year=2012|artist={{w|Meiko (American singer)|Meiko}}|album={{w|The Bright Side (Meiko album)|The Bright Side}}|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UvAi53lynSc|text=I know that it's a secret / And that I gotta '''keep''' it / But I want the lights on / Yeah, I want the lights on}} ## To [[maintain]] (an [[establishment]] or [[institution]]); to [[conduct]]; to [[manage]]. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Twelfth Night|act=III|scene=ii|passage=like a pedant that '''keeps''' a school}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1630|author={{w|John Hayward (historian)|John Hayward}}|title=The Life, and Raigne of King Edward the Sixt|location=London|publisher=John Partridge|page=114|url=http://name.umdl.umich.edu/A02858.0001.001 |passage=They were honourably accompanied and with great estate brought to London, where euery of them '''kept''' house by himselfe.}} ##* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|chapter=III|passage=At half-past nine on this Saturday evening, the parlour of the Salutation Inn, High Holborn, contained most of its customary visitors.{{...}}In former days every tavern of repute '''kept''' such a room for its own select circle, a club, or society, of habitués, who met every evening, for a pipe and a cheerful glass.}} ## To have [[habitually]] in [[stock]] for [[sale]]. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} {{non-gloss|To hold or be held in a state.}} ## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[reside]] for a time; to [[lodge]]; to [[dwell]]. ##: {{ux|en|She '''kept''' to her bed while the fever lasted.}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Titus Andronicus|act=V|scene=ii|passage=Knock at his study, where, they say, he '''keeps''', / To ruminate strange plots of dire revenge; {{...}}}} ## To [[continue]]. ##: {{ux|en|I '''keep''' taking the tablets, but to no avail.}} ##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=XLIV|page=361|passage=Not unnaturally, “Auntie” took this communication in bad part. {{...}} Next day she {{...}} tried to recover her ward by the hair of the head. Then, thwarted, the wretched creature went to the police for help; she was versed in the law, and perhaps had spared no pains to '''keep''' on good terms with the local constabulary.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-28|author=w:Joris Luyendijk |volume=189|issue=3|page=21|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control Our banks are out of control] |passage=Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic{{nb...}}. Until 2008 there was denial over what finance had become.{{...}}But the scandals '''kept''' coming, and so we entered stage three – what therapists call "bargaining". A broad section of the political class now recognises the need for change but remains unable to see the necessity of a fundamental overhaul. Instead it offers fixes and patches.}} ## To [[remain]] [[edible]] or otherwise [[usable]]. ##: {{ux|en|Potatoes can '''keep''' if they are in a [[root cellar]].}} ##: {{ux|en|Latex paint won't '''keep''' indefinitely.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1707|author=[https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Mortimer,_John_(DNB00) John Mortimer]|title=The Whole Art of Husbandry|url=http://books.google.com.au/books?id=8xUAAAAAQAAJ&redir_esc=y |passage=If the malt be not thoroughly dried, the ale it makes will not '''keep'''.}} ## {{lb|en|copulative}} To [[remain]] in a [[state]]. ##: {{ux|en|The rabbit avoided detection by '''keeping''' still.}} ##: {{ux|en|'''Keep''' calm! There's no need to panic.}} ## {{lb|en|UK|obsolete}} To have rooms at college, at the {{w|University of Cambridge}}. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[wait for]], [[keep watch]] for. #* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|10.10|2|VIII|x|passage=And thenne whan the damoysel knewe certaynly that he was not syre launcelot / thenne she took her leue and departed from hym / And thenne syre Trystram rode pryuely vnto the posterne where '''kepte''' hym la beale Isoud / and there she made hym good chere and thanked god of his good spede}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|cricket}} To act as [[wicket-keeper]]. #: {{ux|en|Godfrey Evans '''kept''' for England for many years.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[take care]]; to be [[solicitous]]; to [[watch]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1530|author=w:William Tyndale|chapter=A Pathway into the holy Scripture|title=The Whole Workes of W. Barnes|location=London|publisher=John Day|year_published=1573|page=384|url=http://name.umdl.umich.edu/A68831.0001.001 |passage={{...}} '''kepe''' that the lustes choke not the word of God that is sowen in vs,}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To be [[in session]]; to [[take place]]. #: {{ux|en|School '''keeps''' today.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[observe]]; to [[adhere]] to; to [[fulfill]]; to not [[swerve]] from or [[violate]]. #* {{RQ:King James Version|2 Timothy|4|7|passage=I have '''kept''' the faith: {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=VII|lines=1271–1272|passage=Be strong, live happie, and love, but first of all / Him whom to love is to obey, and '''keep''' / His great command; {{...}}|year=1873}} # {{lb|en|transitive|dated|by extension}} To [[visit]] (a place) often; to [[frequent]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=c. 1608|author={{w|John Fletcher (playwright)|John Fletcher}}|journal=w:The Faithful Shepherdess|section=Act III, Scene 1|url=http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/12222/pg12222-images.html |passage={{...}} 'tis hallowed ground;
